Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1a) demonstrates a solitary, rounded opacity in the right upper lobe with irregular, spiculated margins, which is a classic radiographic appearance suggestive of primary lung carcinoma. The other options describe patterns (fluffy consolidation, air bronchograms, cavitary lesion, miliary nodules) that do not match the discrete, spiculated mass seen in the image.
